state: About 127 open issues of the tool, loop, chaos, paper and owner-task families have no doer: TOOL-FAILURE (15), [self-heal] tool (10), SELF-AUDIT-TOOLERR (3), TOOL-ERROR-RATE (3), CHAOS-DRILL-FAILED-1 (8), FLEET-JOURNEY-FAILED-1 (5), SECRET-CHANGE-OBSERVED (4), PAPER-LEARN-1 (5), PORTFOLIO-GAP (9), WORKFLOW-FAILED-1 (2), OWNER-TASK (59). Their planner verdict 'untrusted' is stale for 32 of them: ops_config.code_merge_trusted_sources was widened on 2026-10-24 and the planner re-reads a non-trusted row only after 7 days.
evidence: READ FIRST, IN FULL: docs/breach-doctor/tool-loop-family-doctor.md (rules R1-R13, findings TL-01..TL-14, anchors verified unique on main), docs/breach-doctor/doctor-sql.sql (every SQL, validated read-only, plus draft migrations NOT applied), docs/breach-doctor/tool-failure-classification.tsv. issue_plans columns: issue_id, planned_at, outcome, detail, task_id, path, model, attempts.

lever.change: PRECONDITION: the BREACH-DOCTOR-1 engine (package breach-doctor-core: migrations/2026-10-26-breach-doctor.sql with tables breach_diagnoses, breach_diagnosis_events, breach_playbooks and the breachDoctorTick block in qnfo-fleet-control/worker.js) is on origin/main when you start. READ that migration and the engine's validator first: a playbook row is data (rule_id, version, family, cause_class, trigger_sql, action_sql JSON array of 1-6 statements each binding ?1 = issue_id, revert_sql JSON array, verify_sql, min_ladder, max_per_tick, max_per_day, enabled, mode, note); the engine validates every statement (one read-only SELECT for trigger/verify; one INSERT/UPDATE on an allowlisted table for action/revert; no reference to the free-text columns description, exceptions_json, cloud_ops_events.text/meta). If the engine is NOT on origin/main, return status 'blocked' with that evidence and change nothing. YOUR CHANGE is a migration of playbook rows (INSERT OR IGNORE into breach_playbooks, mode 'on' for reversible SQL, one row per rule) plus the minimal engine change a rule needs: extending the DOCTOR_WRITE_TABLES allowlist by the tables you write (one const line; another package may extend the same line, so keep your edit to that single line and resolve conflicts by union), cause_class / family code table entries, and tests. Every rule must (1) have a trigger_sql that returns exactly the issues the rule names (run it read-only on live D1 through the Cloudflare MCP and quote the real hit count in the migration comment and in your summary), (2) have a per-issue action that touches only the named issue, (3) have a revert_sql that restores the previous value (stored values come from the facts the trigger returns), (4) have a verify_sql that passes only when the defect is gone, (5) close an issue ONLY by issue_triage.close_evidence built from ids, counts and enum codes (never copied from description/title text), never while an active remediation contract of the issue fails, and (6) be covered by a fixture test that fails without the rule and passes with it, in node:sqlite with the live column lists. A rule you cannot make safe becomes a 'file-issue' playbook or is left out and listed under deviations_from_spec with the reason; never widen the taint rule to make a rule fit. Code-lever rules (one anchored edit in a worker.js) are NOT done here: seed them as agent_issues rows in the same migration with source qnfo-fleet-control, title prefix 'BREACH-DOCTOR-1: <rule_id> <worker>', and `code-task: repo=qnfo-workers path=<dir>/worker.js` plus `code-anchor: <text>` lines, where the anchor was verified byte-exact and unique on current origin/main (quote the count), plus an outcome probe line (runtime-probe or a d1-query contract) that fails while the defect exists and passes only when it is gone, never a code-probe alone. Also add (once, in the first of the three family packages to land; skip if already present) the trusted pair `qnfo-fleet-control|BREACH-DOCTOR-1:` to ops_config code_merge_trusted_sources through a guarded UPDATE that appends only when absent and stores the previous value in an ops_config backup key (read how the 2026-10-21 backup key was written). Do not touch PLAN_TRUSTED code, planner files, qnfo-cloud-ops (claimed by another session) or the dashboard.SCOPE (highest yield first): R1 stale-untrusted-rearm (the 32 issues: UPDATE issue_plans SET planned_at to an old date so the planner re-plans them; the old value goes to revert_sql), R5 tool-signal dedupe (supersede duplicates to the TOOL-FAILURE row with the id as evidence), R3 tool-error classify and exclude (INSERT OR IGNORE into tool_error_exclusions with err_class and rationale for the reviewed literals; allowlist tool_error_exclusions), R9 PAPER-LEARN route, R7 secret-change verification and R8 cf-changelog, R10 workflow-failed (verify the file is absent on main through a stored fact, not free text), R12 owner-task duplicates (supersede exact duplicates with the survivor), R13 loop-breaker; R4 tool-defect code tasks (TD-EMPTY-ERROR, TD-D1Q-REJECT) and R11 stub workers as seeded code-task issues with verified anchors; R2 planner capacity is a code task on qnfo-code-orchestrator (re-plan only when the issue or trust list changed, first-time plans first) seeded as an issue. R6 chaos drills and R14-like items that need a probe repoint go through a migration that repoints the probe, never through a direct security-control write beyond what the doc says. Skip rules the doc marks unproven (TL-14). IDENTITY-BOUND: only OWNER-TASK-op-mvihv5rr376f stays with the owner, as a human_actions card with an IDENTITY-BOUND line and a closing probe if one does not exist.
